business_model.claim: The company is mainly a distributor of propane, renewable propane, RNG, fuel oil and refined fuels. It also markets natural gas and electricity in deregulated markets and produces and invests in low-carbon fuels.
quotes: We specialize in the distribution of propane, renewable propane, renewable natural gas (“RNG”), fuel oil and refined fuels, as well as the marketing of natural gas and electricity in deregulated markets and production of and investing in low-carbon fuel alternatives.

business_model.claim: It serves approximately 1.0 million residential, commercial, industrial and agricultural customers through approximately 750 locations in 42 states.
quotes: As of September 27, 2025, we were serving the energy needs of approximately 1.0 million residential, commercial, industrial and agricultural customers through approximately 750 locations in 42 states with operations principally concentrated in the east and west coast regions of the United States, as well as portions of the midwest region of the United States and Alaska.

business_model.claim: Approximately 93% of propane gallons went to retail customers. Of those gallons, 43% went to residential, 39% to commercial, 8% to industrial, 6% to government and 4% to agricultural customers.
quotes: Approximately 93% of our propane gallons sold in fiscal 2025 were to retail customers: 43% of those propane gallons to residential customers, 39% to commercial customers, 8% to industrial customers, 6% to government customers and 4% to agricultural customers.

business_model.claim: Customer concentration is low: no single customer reached 10% or more of propane revenues.
quotes: No single customer accounted for 10% or more of our propane revenues during fiscal 2025.

business_model.basis: read directly from the 10-Q income statement

business_model.basis: read directly from the 10-Q income statement
business_model.claim: Smaller revenue lines over the same nine months were fuel oil and refined fuels at 62,244, natural gas and electricity at 19,199 and all other at 57,036 (table in thousands).
Under the prior structure, the company managed four operating segments, three of them reportable: Propane, Fuel Oil and Refined Fuels, and Natural Gas and Electricity.
quotes: As described below, we manage and evaluate our operations in four operating segments, three of which are reportable segments: Propane, Fuel Oil and Refined Fuels and Natural Gas and Electricity.

business_model.claim: At the latest fiscal year-end, the company changed to two reportable segments, Propane and Renewable Natural Gas, and recast prior-period segment data to match.
quotes: As a result, the Partnership’s two reportable segments are Propane and Renewable Natural Gas.

business_model.basis: read from the supplemental table in the 8-K release
business_model.claim: Full-year Adjusted EBITDA by segment was Propane $365,928, Renewable Natural Gas $13,519, All other $2,158 and Corporate (97,566), for a total of $284,039.
Profitability depends mainly on the spread between retail selling prices and the cost to acquire and transport product.
quotes: The level of profitability in the retail propane, fuel oil, natural gas and electricity businesses is largely dependent on the difference between retail sales price and our costs to acquire and transport products.

business_model.claim: Propane supply costs are set by index formulas tied to posted prices at major supply points.
quotes: Our propane supply contracts typically provide for pricing based upon index formulas using the posted prices established at major supply points such as Mont Belvieu, Texas, or Conway, Kansas (plus transportation costs) at the time of delivery.

business_model.claim: The company cannot be sure of passing on rapid cost increases fully or immediately, which creates margin risk.
quotes: There is no assurance that we will be able to pass on product acquisition and transportation cost increases fully or immediately, particularly when such costs increase rapidly.

business_model.basis: revenues read from the release table; the price-revenue link is inferred from the release and MD&A
business_model.claim: Revenue moves with commodity prices. Full-year revenues were 1,402,835 versus 1,432,518, while average Mont Belvieu propane prices fell 7.1%.
quotes: Average propane prices (basis Mont Belvieu, Texas) for fiscal 2026 decreased 7.1% compared to the prior year.

business_model.claim: Gross margin excluding mark-to-market adjustments rose $32.7 million, or 3.8%. Drivers were propane unit margins up $0.05 per gallon (2.5%), higher volumes and $12.4 million of PTC benefit.
quotes: Excluding the impact of these unrealized mark-to-market adjustments, gross margin for fiscal 2026 increased $32.7 million, or 3.8%, compared to the prior year, primarily due to an increase in propane unit margins of $0.05 per gallon, or 2.5%, higher propane volumes sold, and the benefit of $12.4 million from PTCs recognized during fiscal 2026 on RNG injections.

business_model.basis: stated in 10-Q MD&A; consistent with the 10-Q income statement
business_model.claim: Demand is seasonal and driven by heating: sales and operating profits are concentrated in the first two fiscal quarters.
quotes: Consequently, sales and operating profits are concentrated in our first and second fiscal quarters.

business_model.claim: Operating cash comes in mainly in the second and third fiscal quarters, as customers pay for winter purchases.
quotes: Cash flows from operations, therefore, are greatest during the second and third fiscal quarters when customers pay for product purchased during the winter heating season.

business_model.claim: Weather drives volumes. The latest fiscal year was 8% warmer than normal and 1% cooler than the prior year, and retail propane gallons of 402.9 million rose approximately 1%.
quotes: Average temperatures (as measured by heating degree days) across all of the Partnership’s service territories for fiscal 2026 were 8% warmer than normal and 1% cooler than the prior year.

business_model.claim: Locations sit where natural gas is not readily available, because propane is generally not competitive with piped natural gas.
quotes: Typically, our customer service centers are located in suburban and rural areas where natural gas is not readily available.

As a result, except for some industrial and commercial applications, propane and fuel oil are generally not economically competitive with natural gas in areas where natural gas pipelines already exist.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K; the retention effect is inferred
business_model.claim: Customer retention is supported by automatic delivery, used by approximately 60% of residential customers, and by company-owned tanks on customer premises.
quotes: Approximately 60% of our residential customers receive their propane supply through an automatic delivery system.
As is common in the propane industry, we own a significant portion of the storage tanks located on our customers’ premises.

business_model.claim: Operating cost lines for the full year were operating 505,567, general and administrative 97,566, cost of products sold 509,450 and depreciation and amortization 67,475.
Combined operating and G&A expense of $603.1 million rose 3.9%. The increase came from payroll and benefits, fuel and vehicle costs and self-insurance accruals.
quotes: The increase was primarily attributable to higher payroll and benefit-related expenses, increased fuel and vehicle maintenance costs, and higher accruals for self-insurance claims, offset to an extent by an insurance recovery related to the partial settlement of certain claims associated with the Partnership’s acquisition of RNG production assets in December 2022.

business_model.claim: Inflation has raised labor, transport, operating and equipment costs.
quotes: Although we have not experienced significant disruptions with securing the products we sell, inflationary factors and competition for resources across the supply chain have resulted in increased costs in a wide variety of areas, including labor, transportation costs, operating costs and the cost of capital expansion projects, tanks and other equipment.

business_model.basis: stated in 10-K MD&A and the 8-K release
business_model.claim: Derivatives are used to hedge inventory and fixed-price sales, not to speculate. Unrealized mark-to-market gains run through cost of products sold.
quotes: Although we use derivative instruments to reduce the effect of price volatility associated with priced physical inventory and forecasted transactions, we do not use derivative instruments for speculative trading purposes.

business_model.claim: RNG output grew: volumes were 369,410 versus 325,702 MMBtu, and average daily injection rose 13% after the Upstate New York digester came online.
quotes: Combined with the contribution from our new anaerobic digester facility in Upstate New York, which was placed into service in July, average daily RNG injection for fiscal 2026 increased 13% compared to the prior year.

business_model.claim: RNG and renewable propane economics depend on environmental attributes and tax credits under federal and state programs.
quotes: The generation and monetization of environmental attributes and available tax credits or other incentives resulting from our production and sale of RNG, and our sale of renewable propane, are contingent on several state and federal programs, including the federal Renewable Fuel Standard program (“RFS”), the Inflation Reduction Act, the One, Big, Beautiful Bill Act, the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, the California Low Carbon Fuel Standard (“CA LCFS”), the Oregon Clean Fuels Program (“OR CFP”), and the Washington Clean Fuel Standard (“WA CFS”).

business_model.claim: The Section 45Z PTC is valued from a base rate of $0.20 per gallon equivalent, adjusted for emissions, volumes and market prices for transferable credits.
quotes: The value of PTCs earned is based on the statutory base credit rate of $0.20 per gallon equivalent, adjusted for applicable prevailing wage and apprenticeship compliance, lifecycle greenhouse gas emissions calculations, qualifying production and sales volumes, and prevailing market prices for transferable tax credits.

business_model.basis: stated in the 8-K release; the run-rate caveat is inferred from the period covered
business_model.claim: The company recognized $12.4 million of PTC benefits and generated $11.3 million of ITCs, but monetized only approximately $3.0 million of PTCs in the year.
quotes: During fiscal 2026, we recognized $12.4 million of benefits from production tax credits (“PTCs”) related to RNG injections for the period from January 2025 through September 2026 and generated $11.3 million of investment tax credits (“ITCs”) associated with qualifying expenditures for the construction of our facility in Upstate New York.
We monetized approximately $3.0 million of the PTCs during fiscal 2026 and expect to monetize the remaining PTCs and the ITCs during fiscal 2027.

business_model.claim: Acquisitions supplement organic growth, including California businesses for $24.0 million and a Florida business for $6.2 million.
quotes: acquiring two well-run businesses in strategic markets in California for $24.0 million and, subsequent to the end of the fiscal year, a high-quality business in Florida for $6.2 million.
